sections.title: STORY OF PROPHET MUSA AND KHIZER (75-82)

translation.text: So they moved on until they came to the people of a town. They asked them for food, but the people refused to give them hospitality. There they found a wall ready to collapse, so the man set it right. Moses protested, “If you wanted, you could have demanded a fee for this.”

commentary.text: The Story of repairing the Wall

After the first two instances they proceeded till they came to the people of a town who were miserly. They asked for food, but the people of the town refused to entertain them. Then they found a wall about to collapse and he (Al-Khidr) fixed it so it was standing upright properly.
At this point, (Musa) questioned Al-Khidr, ‘that since they did not entertain us as guests or give us food then you should not have worked for them for free. You could have asked for wages for the repair done to the wall.’

translation.text: [Al-Khidhr] said, "This is parting between me and you. I will inform you of the interpretation of that about which you could not have patience.

commentary.text: Meaning, because you said after the boy was killed that if you asked me anything after that, you would not accompany me any further. So, this is the parting of the ways between me and you.
The story and the interpretation are given with the greatest economy of words.

translation.text: “As for the ship, it belonged to some poor people, working at sea. So I intended to damage it, for there was a ˹tyrant˺ king ahead of them who seizes every ˹good˺ ship by force.

commentary.text:
Interpretations of why the Ship was damaged
Khidr explains his first action:
‘I damaged the ship to make it faulty so that the oppressive king who would seize every good/working boat by force would not do so.  I wanted to prevent him from taking this boat by making it appear faulty, so that its poor owners who had nothing else could continue to benefit from it.'

translation.text: “And as for the boy, his parents were ˹true˺ believers, and we feared that he would pressure them into defiance and disbelief.

commentary.text:
Interpretation of why the Boy was killed
Khidr explains his second action:
‘And as for the boy, his parents were believers, and that he would oppress them by rebellion and disbelief.’
The boy that Al-Khidr killed was destined to be a disbeliever from the day he was created. The parents love for him might make them follow him in disbelief.

Note: All these actions are done by the command of Allah SWT. Apparently, they are wrong from every aspect including the Sharia however this is Allah SWT’s Will. This is nothing but a mercy for people including the parents.

translation.text: So we hoped that their Lord would give them another, more virtuous and caring in his place.

commentary.text: The son was practically an outlaw-a danger to the public and a particular source of grief to his righteous parents. Even so, his summary capital punishment would have been unjustified if Khidr had been acting on his own. But Khidr was not acting on his own: The plural "we" also implies that he was not acting on his own. He was acting on higher authority and removing a public scourge, who was also become a source of extreme sorrow and humiliation to his parents. His parents are promised a more righteous child who would love them and be a credit to them.

translation.text: “And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the city, and under the wall was a treasure that belonged to them, and their father had been a righteous man. So your Lord willed that these children should come of age and retrieve their treasure, as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it ˹all˺ on my own. This is the explanation of what you could not bear patiently.”

commentary.text: Interpretation of why the Wall was repaired for no Charge

Khidr explains his third action:
‘And as for the wall, it belonged to two orphan boys in the town; and there was a treasure belonging to them (buried underneath the wall). Allah SWT intended that they should attain their age of full strength/maturity and take out their wealth.
‘So your Lord willed..’, is attributed to Allah SWT, because no one else is able to bring them to the age of full strength and puberty except Allah SWT.

Was Al-Khidr a Prophet, human or an angel?
Al-Khidr says, “as a mercy from your Lord. I did not do it ˹all˺ on my own”. Meaning, ‘I was only commanded to do the things that were enjoined upon me by Allah SWT.’ So Al-Khidr did not take any action on his own accord.
Thus, this is the explanation of the things which (Musa) could not be patient with.

sections.title: STORY OF KING ZUL-QARNAIN (83-101)

translation.text: And they ask you, [O Muhammad], about Zul-Qarnain. Say, "I will recite to you about him a report."

commentary.text: This is a continuation of the questions the disbelievers of Makkah who, in consultation with the people of the Book, had put to Muhammad (PBUH) as a test of his Prophethood. Who is Zul-Qarnain?
Here the core or theme of this ruku is that power, authority, respect, is all given by Allah SWT as a test. Never become unjust or oppressive as a ruler or master.
The Story of Zul-Qarnain

Zul- Qarnain was Cyrus, an ancient king of Iran. 
Now let us consider the characteristics of Zul-Qarnain in the light of his story as given in the Quran.

(1) The title Zul-Qarnain (the two-horned).
(2) Zul-Qarnain was a great ruler and conqueror. Allah SWT gave him righteousness, stability, strength, authority and power. 
(3) He constructed a strong wall across a mountain pass to protect his kingdom from the incursions of Gog and Magog. 
(4) Besides possessing the above-mentioned characteristics, he was also a righteous servant of Allah SWT and a just ruler, for the Quran has brought into prominence these characteristics more than anything else.

translation.text: until he reached the setting ˹point˺ of the sun, which appeared to him to be setting in a spring of murky water, where he found some people. We said, “O Ⱬul-Qarnain! Either punish them or treat them kindly.”

commentary.text: Zul-Qarnain conquered huge territories including a land on the extreme west of the earth, that is, when he saw the sun as if it were setting in the ocean.

We (Allah) said (by inspiration):"O Zul-Qarnain! Either you punish them or treat them with kindness." Allah SWT gave him power over them and gave him the choice: if he wanted to, he could kill the men and take the women and children captive, or if he wanted to, he could set them free, with or without a ransom. His justice and faith became apparent in the ruling he pronounced (below).

translation.text: He responded, “Whoever does wrong will be punished by us, then will be returned to their Lord, Who will punish them with a horrible torment.

commentary.text: ‘Whoever does wrong will be punished by us…’, meaning who persists in Kufr and in associating others in worship with his Lord, shall be punished by death.  Then Allah SWT will punish him with a more severe, far-reaching and painful punishment.

translation.text: As for those who believe and do good, they will have the finest reward, and we will assign them easy commands.”

commentary.text: IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS

translation.text: until he reached the rising ˹point˺ of the sun. He found it rising on a people for whom We had provided no shelter from it.

commentary.text: Zul-Qarnain then traveled from the west of the earth towards the east. Every time he passed a nation, he subjugated the people and called them to Allah SWT.

When he reached the place where the sun rises meaning a nation for whom Allah SWT provided no shelter or shade against the sun because, they had no buildings or trees to cover them or shade them from the heat of the sun.

translation.text: until he reached ˹a pass˺ between two mountains. He found in front of them a people who could hardly understand ˹his˺ language.

commentary.text: Then he followed (another) way. Until, when he reached between two mountains, meaning, he traveled from the east of the earth until he reached a place between the two mountains which were next to one another with a valley in between, from which Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog) will emerge into the land of the Turks and spread mischief there, destroying crops and people.

translation.text: They pleaded, “O Ⱬul-Qarnain! Surely Gog and Magog are spreading corruption throughout the land. Should we pay you tribute, provided that you build a wall between us and them?”

commentary.text: Here Gog and Magog were causing much corruption and chaos in the land. The people wanted a wall to be built as a barrier against them. (This is a small mention much before the DoJ)
Also see Surah Al-Anbya Ayat 96
until ˹after˺ Gog and Magog have broken loose ˹from the barrier˺, swarming down from every hill,
(This is the mention closer to the DoJ)

translation.text: Bring me blocks of iron!” Then, when he had filled up ˹the gap˺ between the two mountains, he ordered, “Blow!” When the iron became red hot, he said, “Bring me molten copper to pour over it.”

commentary.text: A strong barrier/wall of iron, with fortified iron gates was constructed and the spaces filled up with molten lead, so as to form an impregnable mass of metal.

translation.text: So Gog and Magog were unable to pass over it, nor were they able [to effect] in it any penetration.

commentary.text: The iron wall was sufficiently high and smooth (slick) so as to prevent their Gog and Magog from either scaling it or attempting to dig through it.

translation.text: He declared, “This is a mercy from my Lord. But when the promise of my Lord comes to pass, He will level it to the ground. And my Lord’s promise is ever true.”

commentary.text: He declared, “This is a mercy from my Lord..’, that is, after all the effort which Zul-Qarnain made for their protection, he claimed no credit for himself beyond that of discharging his duty as a ruler.

sections.title: FATE OF THE MUSHRIKIN AND THE BELIEVERS ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT (102-108)

translation.text: Say, (O Muhammad): "Shall We tell you who will be the greatest losers in respect of their works?

commentary.text: This ruku discusses how when man becomes lost in this world and its glitter, glamor, entertainment etc., then that is when we are committing the biggest kufr. This world has made you oblivious to the Hereafter. Some feel that is Dajjal.

The Ayat is general and refers to everyone who worships Allah SWT in a way that is not acceptable, thinking that he is doing right and that his deeds will be accepted. Their loss is all the greater because they had a misplaced confidence in their own deeds or in the assistance of false "protectors".

Also see 25:23
And We shall turn to whatever deeds they did, and We shall make such deeds as scattered floating particles of dust.

Also see 24:39
As for those who disbelieved, their deeds are like a mirage in a desert. The thirsty one thinks it to be water, until he comes up to it, he finds it to be nothing.

translation.text: ˹They are˺ those whose efforts are in vain in this worldly life, while they think they are doing good!”

commentary.text: Those who limit all their endeavors to this worldly life meaning that whatever good they do, they do for this world without paying any regard to God and the Hereafter, these are the people who despite their relentless efforts are the greatest losers. So, for example, charity is given to impress people or outward show and not with the intent to please Allah SWT. Thus, deeds done without the intention of please Allah SWT and not in accordance to the sunnah have no merit.
The sad part is that they think they are doing the best actions and that their efforts are the finest.
Lesson: Decide is you are a seeker of this world or the seeker of the Hereafter.

translation.text: It is they who reject the signs of their Lord and their meeting with Him, rendering their deeds void, so We will not give their deeds any weight on Judgment Day.

commentary.text: People who reject Allah SWT and the Hereafter, then whatever good they do will be of not value to them in the life after death, even though they might have considered these deeds their greatest achievements but the fact is that they will lose all their value as soon as the world shall come to an end.

When they will go before their Lord, and all their deeds shall be placed in the scales, they will have no weight at all whether they had built great palaces, established great universities and libraries, set up great factories and laboratories, constructed highways and railways, in short, all their inventions, industries, sciences and arts and other things of which they were very proud in this world, will lose their weights in the scales.
The only thing which will have weight there will be that which had been done in accordance with the divine instructions and with the intention to please Allah.
Lesson: Realize this world is a fleeting moment in time and the real life is yet to be experienced. Choose wisely.

translation.text: Indeed, those who have believed and done righteous deeds - they will have the Gardens of Paradise as a lodging,

sections.title: WORDS OF ALLAH ARE COUNTLESS AND CANNOT BE RECORDED (109)

translation.text: Say: "If the sea were to become ink to record the Words of my Lord, indeed the sea would be all used up before the Words of my Lord are exhausted, and it would be the same even if We were to bring an equal amount of ink."

sections.title: MUHAMMAD IS BUT A HUMAN BEING LIKE YOU (110)

translation.text: Say, ˹O Prophet,˺ “I am only a man like you, ˹but˺ it has been revealed to me that your God is only One God. So whoever hopes for the meeting with their Lord, let them do good deeds and associate none in the worship of their Lord.”

commentary.text: Muhammad is a Human Being and a Messenger, and the God is One
Prophet Muhammad is being told to tell people that he is a human just like them but the only difference is that ‘wahi or revelation is sent to him by Allah SWT.
IMAN + GOOD DEEDS = SUCCESS
Whomever is hoping and looking forward to meeting their Lord (i) DO GOOD DEEDS (DONE IN THE PRESCRIBED MANNER) AND (ii) DO NOT DO SHIRK.

And there are some interesting anchors between the first story and the third and then the second story with the fourth.

Lessons:
Resilience of faith despite the pressures of society/family etc. and reliance on Allah SWT alone.
Keep good company. And understand the definition of good company as defined by Allah SWT. (18:28)
Do not get caught up in the glitz and glamour of this fleeting world instead focus on the end game.
Do not speculate on issues that you do not know about or that do not concern you rather focus on the tasks at hand. (18:19) (18:22)
FYI – One of the questions we will be asked on the DoJ is how we spent our youth?

Allah SWT tells us exactly what to say rather than speculate. (18:26)

And do not obey those whose hearts We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follow ˹only˺ their desires and whose state is ˹total˺ loss.
SECOND STORY OF THE TWO GARDENS AND THE PARABLE OF A BELIEVER AND A DISBELIEVER
Lessons:
We are being tested in this life with abundance as well as the lack of it. (Trial of wealth)

Place your trust in Allah SWT alone and not creation nor yourself.  Allah SWT is our Wali. He is the best Provider and Planner. People tend to place all faith and trust in material/money and forget Allah SWT. This is the shirk of our time as opposed to idol or sun worship.
Upon receiving Allah SWT’s blessing remain humble, grateful and remember Allah SWT much.
Duas from Allah SWT for mankind
Allah SWT tells us exactly what to say when we see something that pleases us from our wealth or our children. (18: 39)
(18:32) Set forth to them the parable of two men: for one of them We provided two gardens of grape-vines and surrounded them with date palms; in between the two We placed corn-fields.

Second section: two stories: (i) Musa and Al-Khidr (ii) Dhul-Qarnayn
FIRST STORY ABOUT MUSA AND Al-KHIDR
Lessons:
In this world although we may find something apparently bad or objectionable there is a wisdom of Allah SWT. Understand and appreciate what Allah SWT has decreed or destined for us.

Al-Khidr was humble, grateful and acknowledged all his wisdom and guidance was from Allah SWT alone. (18:82) Thus attributing and acknowledging that all guidance and wisdom is bestowed upon mankind by Allah SWT.
Musa immediately apologized and asked for pardon/leniency. He was not argumentative and suborn. Remember Allah SWT seals the hearts of those who are obstinate, stubborn and refuse to believe.

Again, the concept of asking needless questions is being repeated as was the case in the first story. Questions in religion should be to either strengthen ones iman/faith or strengthen one’s practice. Curiosity that neither benefit iman or action/amal is outside the realm of guidance or sincere counsel. So, although we should be curious ideally it should be caged in what is most beneficial.

Musa was commanded by Allah SWT to travel to one of his servants who had knowledge which Musa had not been granted. Al-Khidr had made the condition that Musa should not ask him about anything he found objectionable until he (Al-Khidr) himself initiated the discussion and offered an explanation.
Damaging the Boat
So, they went on board the ship. When the boat took was out to sea and they were far from the shore, Al-Khidr got up and damaged the boat, pulling out one of its planks.

‘I damaged the ship to make it faulty so that the oppressive king who would seize every good/working boat by force would not do so.

They continued after the first incident, till they met a boy, and he (Al Khidr) killed him.

translation.text: He said: "Lord! My bones have grown feeble and my head is glistening with age; yet, never have my prayers to You, my Lord, been unfruitful.

commentary.text:
The story of Zakariya and his dua for a son
Prophet Zakariya, who is about 100 years old and his wife barren, is worried about the fact that there is no one who is religiously and morally capable of carrying on the work entrusted to him. Zakariya (PBUH) asks Allah SWT (with full faith of a positive response) for an heir to pass on this knowledge.
Hadith: Call upon Allah SWT in private, humbly and with full faith. Best to make dua in prostration so its just between you and Allah SWT.

translation.text: He answered: "So shall it be." Your Lord says: "It is easy for Me," and then added: "For beyond doubt, I created you earlier when you were nothing."

commentary.text: Allah SWT is able to do whatever He wills with ease. Zakariya, despite his old age and barren wife is blessed with a righteous, and purified son called Yaya (named by Allah SWT).

translation.text: Zechariah said: "Lord, grant me a Sign." Said He: "Your Sign is that you shall not be able to speak to people for three nights, though you will be otherwise sound."

commentary.text: During these three days of silence Zakariya increased his righteous deeds and gratitude towards Allah SWT. (Zakariya was happy and excited so could have wasted this precious time in idle talk).

The qualities bestowed on Yaya: (i) Wisdom, compassion and kindness (ii) Allah consciousness (taqwa) and intense love for Allah SWT (iii) purity of character (no jealousy and the ability to forgive) (iv) dutiful to parents (v) not arrogant.
Lesson: Always be mindful of the human characteristics Allah SWT references so as to try and attain them.

The story of Maryam

translation.text: (O Muhammad), recite in the Book the account of Abraham. Most surely he was a man of truth, a Prophet.

commentary.text: Story of  Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH)

From here the address is directed towards the people of Makkah who had forced their own near and dear relatives to emigrate from their homes. Similarly, Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) was forced to leave his nation and family by his own father and brethren. The story of Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) has been selected here because the Quraish accepted him as their religious leader and were proud of being his descendants.

Allah SWT did not disappoint – He blessed Prophet Ibrahim (PBUH) with a good mention for eternity and blessed him with pious children and grandchildren.

Every person will beg Allah SWT to give them one more day in this world to make things right. Wasted moments will be the biggest source of regret. Just sitting around wasting time.

front_matter.label: Name
front_matter.text: This Surah takes its name from its "first word "Ta Ha." This name, like the names of many other Surahs, is merely symbolic.

items.text: طٰهٰ ۚ

front_matter.label: Period of Revelation
front_matter.text: This is a Makki Surah that was revealed sometime before the Hijrah to Abyssinia. This Surah has 135 verses in 8 Rukus.

front_matter.label: Subjects and Topics
front_matter.text:
The subject matter of the Surah is to assure the Prophet and his followers that the message of the Quran will eventually succeed.
The story of Prophet Musa (PBUH) is mentioned in detail. The ultimate outcome of those who were vehemently opposing Islam is also described.

sections.title: 1 - 8  AL-QURAN IS A REMINDER FOR THOSE WHO FEAR ALLAH, THE CREATOR OF THE HEAVENS AND EARTH

translation.text: Ta' Ha'
We did not reveal the Qur'an to you to cause you distress;
it is only a reminder for him who fears Allah;

commentary.text: The Quran is a Reminder and a Revelation from Allah

The object of the revelation of the Quran is not to distress the Prophet (PBUH) by demanding from him to fill the hearts of the stubborn people with faith, rather to caution those people who have fear of Allah SWT. Quran is the most precious gift to us from Allah SWT so do not make it a burden. These are the words and speech of our Raab.
Lesson: When giving dawah do not waste your efforts on those who have no fear of God left in them and who do not bother at all about what is truth and what is falsehood.

sections.title: 9 - 16 PROPHET MUSA WENT TO THE SACRED VALLEY OF 'TUWA' AT MOUNT TUR

intro.text: From this point begins the story of Prophet Musa (PBUH), and how revelation came to him with Allah SWT speaking directly to him.

After Musa had completed the agreed upon contract between his father-in-law and himself to herd sheep, he then left to return to the land of Egypt.  However, on the way he and his wife lost their way on a cold, wintry night. They made camp between some mountain passes that were covered with snow, sleet, dense clouds, darkness and fog. Musa repeatedly and unsuccessfully attempted to make fire when he saw a fire from the side of the mountain. It appeared to him to be a fire glowing from the right side of the mountain from where he was and he went towards it.

translation.text: When he came to it, a voice called out: "Moses!
Verily I am your Lord! Take off your shoes.7 You are in the sacred valley, Tuwa!
I Myself have chosen you; therefore, give ear to what is revealed.

arabic_lines: اِنَّنِىۡۤ اَنَا اللّٰهُ لَاۤ اِلٰهَ اِلَّاۤ اَنَا فَاعۡبُدۡنِىۡ ۙ وَاَقِمِ الصَّلٰوةَ لِذِكۡرِىۡ

translation.text: Verily I am Allah. There is no god beside Me. So serve Me and establish Prayers to remember Me.

commentary.text: There is no other place in the Quran where Allah SWT displayed his authority in the first person.

The real objective of Salat is mentioned here. It has been prescribed to remind people that they should not become neglectful of Allah SWT by worldly diversions and that they should remember that man is not an unbridled free being but a servant of Allah SWT. Salat has been prescribed five times a day to remind man of Allah’ SWTs authority and presence.
Hadith: Whenever one of you sleeps past the prayer, or he forgets to pray, then let him pray when he remembers it.

sections.title: 17 - 24 ALLAH CHOSE HIM AS HIS RASOOL AND ASSIGNED HIM TOWARDS PHARAON (PHARAOH)

intro.text: Allah SWT told Prophet Musa to invite Pharaon to the Exclusive worship of Allah SWT, and to treat the Children of Israel well and not torment them. Indeed Pharaon transgressed all limits claiming that he was god, oppressed, preferred the worldly life and forgotten his Master. Allah SWT equipped Musa with two miracles to show Pharaon and his people.

Lesson: Whenever Allah SWT gives us a task or some adversity He also equips us with the tools to deal with the situation.  We are never alone so call upon Allah SWT as did Musa (PBUH) at your time of need. Allah SWT is very close and hears.

sections.title: 25 - 48 PROPHET MUSA PRAYED TO ALLAH TO OPEN HIS HEART, EASY HIS TASK AND REMOVE THE IMPEDIMENT FROM HIS SPEECH SO THAT PEOPLE MAY UNDERSTAND, WHAT HE SAYS -ALLAH GRANTED HIS REQUEST AND REMINDED MUSA OF HIS FAVORS

intro.text: Prophet Musa (PBUH) asked Allah SWT for courage and confidence because he was aware and conscious of the fact that he was not a eloquent speaker. Below is the dua for fluency/clarity of speech.

translation.text: Musa (PBUH) said: "Lord! Open my breast for me
and ease my task for me
and loosen the knot from my tongue
so that they may understand my speech

commentary.text: This dua should be memorized for all situations but especially when giving dawa.

translation.text: Recall, when your sister went along, saying: 'Shall I direct you to one who will take charge of him?' Thus We brought you back to your mother so that her heart might be gladdened and she might not grieve.

commentary.text: Musa (PBUH), recall when you slew a person. We delivered you from distress and made you go through several trials. Then you stayed for several years among the people of Midian, and now you have come at the right moment as ordained.
Then you did kill a man, but We saved you from great distress and tried you with a heavy trial

Allah SWT recounted the many trials and tribulations Musa (PBUH) went through during his life -- from the time he was a baby and his mother had to cast him into the river, how Musa killed a man (accidently), the many years he lived in Madina and then how he was at the right place at the right time as decreed by Allah SWT to see the fire.

translation.text: I have chosen you for My service.

commentary.text: Allah SWT says, "I have manufactured/chosen/nurtured/trained you for a particular task." Thus, nothing is other than as it has been ordained.

Lesson: Nothing in life is random. Prophet Musa's life was difficult but Allah SWT was training him for a task only he could perform. We should accept our decree happily and look forward to the future.

sections.title: 49 - 54 DIALOGUE BETWEEN MUSA AND PHARAON

intro.text: Allah SWT choose Musa to go to Pharaon and instructed him to be Soft and Gentle in His Invitation
Two ways to give dawah are:( 1 ) To convince by argument and (2) to caution or warn of the consequences of deviation.

translation.text: [Pharaoh] said, ‘Moses, who is this Lord of yours?’
He answered, “Our Lord is the One Who has given everything its ˹distinctive˺ form, then guided ˹it˺.”
translation.ref_as_written: printed 20:49 twice; from context the second is 20:50

commentary.text: What a beautiful, concise and meaningful introduction to Allah SWT – He is Our creator and then Our guider.

translation.text: Pharaoh asked: "Then, what is the state of the former generations?"

commentary.text: Pharon asked a controversial question so that everyone listening should doubt and get offended by Musa (PBUH). He asked about the former generations. Their ancestors, whom they took so much pride in, did not worship Allah instead worshipped other gods/deities.

translation.text: Moses said, ‘My Lord alone has knowledge of them, all in a record; my Lord does not err or forget.’

commentary.text: This answer is full of wisdom. Prophet Musa (PBUH) did not say: Yes, they all lacked common sense, went astray and now are the fuel of Hell. Nor did he say they are all in Heaven because they are all children of Allah SWT.

His answer was to this effect: Well, those people have now gone before their Lord, and I have no means of judging their deeds and intentions. However, their whole record is safe and secure with Allah, and nothing can escape Him. Allah alone knows how to deal with them. What concerns you and me is our own position and attitude to life. We should be more concerned about our own end than of those who have already passed away into Allah SWT's presence.

Lesson: Prophet Musa (PBUH) was instructed by Allah SWT to speak gently to the Pharaoh. This is a strategy we should follow as well especially when giving dawah. Always speak nobly, gently and begin with commonalities, however, if the other is not ready to receive then STOP! Do not get baited into controversy and semantics.

sections.title: 55 - HUMAN LIFE CYCLE

intro.text: The earth is your beginning, that is, Adam, was created with dirt from the surface of the earth. Then when we die we are returned to the ground to become dirt again. So why assume arrogance?

sections.title: 56 - 64 PHARAON DISBELIEVED MUSA BY CALLING HIS MIRACLES A MAGICIAN TRICK AND CHALLENGED HIM TO CONFRONT HIS MAGICIANS IN PUBLIC - MUSA ACCEPTED THE CHALLENGE
65 - 76 CONFRONTATION OF MUSA AND PHARAON'S MAGICIANS, AFTER WITNESSING MUSA'S MIRACLE MAGICIANS ACCEPTED ISLAM

arabic_lines: وَاَ لۡقِ مَا فِىۡ يَمِيۡنِكَ تَلۡقَفۡ مَا صَنَعُوۡا ؕاِنَّمَا صَنَعُوۡا كَيۡدُ سٰحِرٍ ؕ وَلَا يُفۡلِحُ السّٰحِرُ حَيۡثُ اَتٰى

translation.text: Cast what is in your right hand, and it will swallow up what they have made, for what they have made is no more than a magic trick. And magicians can never succeed wherever they go.

commentary.text: Practicing magic is Kufur and seeking help from satan. Stay away from all things magic. Magicians accepted Islam. When someone accepts Islam all his or her previous sins are erased. It is as if they are beginning anew.

FYI – When asked if he wanted to take his turn first in the competition Prophet Musa (PBUH) declined. Always best to let your challenger/opponent go first so as to understand and observe before embarking of a task.

translation.text: But whoever comes to Him (Allah) as a believer, and has done righteous good deeds, for such are the high ranks

commentary.text: Iman + Good deeds = Success
Just to say I believe or provide lip service is not enough rather one has to actively strive hard with good and righteous  deeds i.e. in the form of salah, fasting, charity, etc.

Hadith: The Prophet (PBUH) said, Paradise has one hundred levels and between each level is a distance like the distance between the sky and the earth. Al-Firdaws is the name of the highest of its levels and above it is Allah SWT's throne. Therefore, when you ask Allah SWT for Heaven always ask for Al-Firdaws.

sections.title: 77 - 82 DELIVERANCE OF THE CHILDREN OF ISRAEL FROM THE BONDAGE OF PHARAON

translation.text: O children of Israel, We rescued you from your enemy and fixed a time for your attendance on the right side of Tur, and sent down manna and salva to you. Eat of the pure provision We have given you and do not transgress after this; otherwise My wrath will visit you.

commentary.text: Allah SWT sent down manna and salva for the people of Israel when Musa (PBUH) went to receive the Torah. They were told not to save anything for the next day. Don’t hoard or be greedy instead have full faith and trust (tawaqul) in Allah SWT. Greediness, obsession with this world, selfishness, hoarding all becomes a source of humiliation in this world and the next. One falls in the sight of Allah SWT as well as people.

translation.text: Yet I am most forgiving towards those who repent, believe, do righteous deeds, and stay on the right path.

commentary.text: Iman + Good deeds = Success

sections.title: 83 - 89 WHEN PROPHET MUSA WENT TO MOUNT TUR FOR COMMUNION WITH ALLAH - ISRAELITES STARTED WORSHIPPING CALF IN HIS ABSENCE
90 - 98 MUSA'S INQUIRY ABOUT THE IDOL WORSHIPPING, HIS DECISION ABOUT SAMIRI, GOLDEN CALF AND HIS ADDRESS TO HIS PEOPLE

intro.text: When Musa returned with the Torah he found the BI worshipping a golden calf. Allah SWT is constantly testing us as He tested nations before us. The golden calf did not just appear rather each individual fulfilled his/her part in helping accomplish this goal. Nothing just happens in life rather we actively participate in making good or bad decisions taking one step at a time. Therefore, "it just happened." is not an acceptable excuse. Make choices wisely as every decision will have consequences.

Samiri's punishment was either a social boycott or a disease (some say when anyone came near him both the person and Samiri developed a high fever) whereby no one came near him. All his life he was alone – an outcast, social leper.
The golden calf was burnt and its ashes scattered.

arabic_lines: اِنَّمَاۤ اِلٰهُكُمُ اللّٰهُ الَّذِىۡ لَاۤ اِلٰـهَ اِلَّا هُوَؕ وَسِعَ كُلَّ شَىۡءٍ عِلۡمًا

translation.text: Your God is none else than Allah, beside Whom there is no god. His knowledge embraces everything.

commentary.text: Allah SWT reminds us that there is only one Allah. The message of Tauhid.

sections.title: 99 - 104 AL-QURAN IS BUT A REMINDER AND THE LIFE OF THIS WORLD SHALL APPEARS TO BE NO LONGER THAN ONE DAY IN THE HEREAFTER

translation.text: This is how We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of the past. And We have certainly granted you a Reminder from Us.
Whoever turns away from it will surely bear the burden ˹of sin˺ on the Day of Judgment.

commentary.text: Here the story of Prophet Musa (PBUH) comes to an end. Now comes the resumption of the theme introduced in the very beginning of the surah, that is, the Quran has not been sent down to put the Holy Prophet in distress, rather it was an Admonition for the God-fearing. 1 - 8  AL-QURAN IS A REMINDER FOR THOSE WHO FEAR ALLAH, THE CREATOR OF THE HEAVENS AND EARTH.

It is imperative that our connection and relationship with the Quran (Allah SWT's words) be given the utmost priority, as it will either lead to our eternal success or eternal failure. Turning away from the Quran in essence means purposely rejecting it. Make the learning, understanding, reciting, and implementation of the Quran the biggest priority in life – and do it now before it is too late!

sections.title: 105 - 112 A SCENE FROM THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

intro.text: The earth will be leveled i.e. mountains turned to dust and oceans dried up. The disbelievers will be raised up from their graves sightless/blind (just like they were in life – blind to the truth).

Those who reject the Quran and its guidance in this world only harm themselves as punishment is around the corner – sooner than one thinks. On the DoJ when Allah SWT will ask, 'For how many years did you stay on the Earth?' The disbelievers will say, 'We stayed there for a day - or a part of a day. It is clear that they will consider both the life on the earth and the life in the interval between death and Resurrection to be very short.

Now contrary to their expectations they have to face eternal life of the Hereafter that they denied all their worldly life. They will wring their hands with regret (Day of Judgment as called Day of Regret) that they ruined their eternal life for the sake of a few transitory pleasures of the short life they were given on Earth.

arabic_lines: وَعَنَتِ الۡوُجُوۡهُ لِلۡحَىِّ الۡقَيُّوۡمِؕ وَقَدۡ خَابَ مَنۡ حَمَلَ ظُلۡمًا

translation.text: All faces shall be humbled before the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting Lord, and he who bears the burden of iniquity will have failed

commentary.text: Ya  Hayyu Ya Qayyumm – these are the two names of Allah SWT that have come together three times in the Quran – (i) Surah Al Bakara in Ayat ul Kursi, (ii) beginning of Surah Al-Imran, and now. These two names are also called Ismu Azam or Allah SWT best names. It is said that whomever makes a dua using these two names of Allah SWT then their dua is accepted.

arabic_lines: وَمَنۡ يَّعۡمَلۡ مِنَ الصّٰلِحٰتِ وَهُوَ مُؤۡمِنٌ فَلَا يَخٰفُ ظُلۡمًا وَّلَا هَضۡمًا

translation.text: but whosoever does righteous works, being a believer, shall have no fear of suffering wrong or loss.

commentary.text: Iman + Good deeds = Success

sections.title: 113 - 115 AL-QURAN IS SENT IN ARABIC TO TEACH AND TO REMIND, SO READ AND SAY, "O RABB INCREASE MY KNOWLEDGE"

arabic_lines: فَتَعٰلَى اللّٰهُ الۡمَلِكُ الۡحَـقُّ ۚ وَلَا تَعۡجَلۡ بِالۡقُرۡاٰنِ مِنۡ قَبۡلِ اَنۡ يُّقۡضٰٓى اِلَيۡكَ وَحۡيُهٗ وَقُلْ رَّبِّ زِدۡنِىۡ عِلۡمًا

translation.text: Exalted is Allah, the True King! Hasten not with reciting the Qur'an before its revelation to you is finished, and pray: "Lord! Increase me in knowledge."

commentary.text: Beautiful dua asking Allah SWT to increase us in our knowledge and Iman of the Quran so that we can fully comprehend and appreciate the complexity, intensity and magnificence of His guidance.

sections.title: 116 - 128 STORY OF ADAM'S CREATION AND SHAITAN'S TEMPTATION AND ALLAH FORGAVE ADAM'S SIN, CHOSE HIM AND GUIDED HIM TO THE RIGHT WAY AND THOSE WHO DO NOT READ AL-QURAN AND FOLLOW ITS GUIDANCE SHALL BE RAISE AS BLIND ON THE DAY OF RESURRECTION

translation.text: But Satan seduced him, saying: "Adam! Shall I direct you to a tree of eternal life and an abiding kingdom?

Then the two of them ate the fruit of that tree and their shameful parts became revealed to each other, and they began to cover themselves with the leaves from the Garden. Thus Adam disobeyed his Lord and strayed into error.

commentary.text: Although Allah SWT accepted Adam and Eve's repentance, yet, they were expelled from Heaven and sent to Earth.

Remember: Sins have consequences. With repentance, in sha Allah, sins are forgiven, however, each sin has a consequence that we will have to suffer/endure in this world, for example, a car accident means we have to pay the cost of damage/hospital etc. Thus, there is a consequence of our negligence.

So realize your blessings and do everything to preserve your blessings because satan is a clear enemy always striving to lead us astray. Follow Allah SWT's guidance for success in this life and the next.

translation.text: But whoever turns away from My Reminder will certainly have a miserable life, then We will raise them up blind on the Day of Judgment.

commentary.text: A miserable life in this world does not mean a life of poverty rather it refers to a lack of peace of mind. Despite money, power, success those who turn away from Allah SWT's guidance will be deprived of their peace of mind and real happiness in this world -- as well as the next.
On the Day of Judgment the disbelievers will be raised sightless (even though they could see perfectly in the world) because they were blinded, heedless or chose to ignore guidance in this world.

translation.text: This is how We reward whoever transgresses and does not believe in the revelations of their Lord. And the punishment of the Hereafter is far more severe and more lasting.

commentary.text: Allah SWT is no doubt 'Rehman' and 'Rahim' (forgiving and merciful) but also remember that punishment is severe for those who transgress.
Transgression + Disbelief = Eternal punishment

sections.title: 129 - 132 DO NOT ENVY OTHERS IN WORLDLY BENEFITS RATHER SEEK ALLAH'S PLEASURE IF YOU WANT TO ATTAIN THE BLESSED END

translation.text: So bear patiently with what they say. Glorify your Lord, praising Him before sunrise and before sunset, and in the watches of the night, and glorify Him and at the ends of the day that you may attain to happiness.

commentary.text: Prophet (PBUH) is being advised to bear patiently all the taunting and abuse he was suffering at the hands of the disbelievers.

Solution to troubles in this world: (i) Be patient, (ii) Be steadfast in your prayers and  (iii) keep your tongue moist with Allah SWT's zikr especially at the time before sunrise and sunset. This is the recipe for success and happiness.

translation.text: And do not gaze longingly at what We have given some of them to enjoy, the finery of this present life: We test them through this, but the provision of your Lord is better and more lasting.

commentary.text: This is an address to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) and thus by default to all of us; that it does not behoove you to be envious of the riches and wealth that people are amassing. The very best things of this life are nothing compared with the good of the Hereafter.

Provisions and finery of this world are nothing but a test and trial bestowed by Allah SWT on all his servants regardless of whether they believe or not. However, the special provision of Allah SWT (taqwa, guidance, knowledge and Iman) is reserved for his devoted servants and incomparably more valuable and everlasting. So do not stare longingly with desire at things others have, as it is not worth putting all your effort in attaining them.

translation.text: Enjoin Prayer on your household, and do keep observing it. We do not ask you for any worldly provision; rather, it is We who provide you, and ultimately the pious will end up the best.

commentary.text: Command your family to pray and be steadfast in your own prayer. People learn from example more than words. Seek all your provisions from Allah SWT.
Piousness/Piety/Righteousness = Success

sections.title: 133 - 135 AL-QURAN IS A SIGN FROM ALLAH SO THERE CAN BE NO EXCUSE FOR THE UNBELIEVERS ON THE DAY OF JUDGEMENT

translation.text: [Prophet], say, ‘We are all waiting, so you carry on waiting: you will come to learn who has followed the even path, and been rightly guided.’

commentary.text: The Prophet (PBUH) who is being tortured and taunted at the hands of the kufar is being told to be patient as soon all things will become clear.

Lesson: No matter how stressful a situation a Believer remains steadfast and gets his/her strength through prayers and zikr. Stop looking towards others for validation or as competition, as this is a recipe for a miserable life. Time is a limited resource so do not waste it in capturing this world. Satan loves to see us when we are sad, unhappy, jealous and envious as this is when our focus is taken away from worship. Remember: what is meant for you will always come to you.
(i) Patience (ii) Prayers (obligatory and optional) (iii) Zikr & tasbeeh are all ingredients for success.

WHY IS THE QURAN CALLED A REMINDER
(20:2) We did not reveal the Quran to you to cause you distress;
(20:3) it is only a reminder for him who fears Allah;
(20:99) This is how We relate to you ˹O Prophet˺ some of the stories of the past. And We have certainly granted you a Reminder from Us.

Quran is called a 'reminder' for mankind because Allah SWT has placed within us a natural instinct also called 'fitra.' The teachings of the Quran are meant to awaken our fitrah and remind us of things that we instinctively know but have cast aside. Neglect, heedlessness, ignorance, distractions, etc., all dim the light of fitrah that then the verses of Quran try to awaken. Regular tilāwah (recitation) of the Quran help us overcome neglect and heedlessness.
Significance of stories of the past in the Quran

Quran relates stories of the past so that we may take heed as well as get motivated. A smart person learns from the mistakes of others as well as gets inspired by others. The same arguments for shirk that were given in the past are being parroted today, thus, there is nothing new that is taking place today that did not take place thousands of years ago. Learn from the past.
CONSEQUENCES OF NEGLECTING THE QURAN (ALLAH SWT'S REMINDER)
(20:124) But whoever turns away from My Reminder will certainly have a miserable life, then We will raise them up blind on the Day of Judgment.
Consequences of neglecting the Quran (My Reminder) :

A miserable life in this world does not mean a life of poverty, rather it refers to a lack of peace of mind. Despite having money, power, and success those who turn away from Allah SWT will be deprived of peace of mind and real happiness in this world -- as well as the next. On the DoJ they will be raised blind as they were blinded to guidance in this world.

It is imperative that our connection and relationship with the Quran (Allah SWT's words) be given the utmost priority, as it will either lead to our eternal success or eternal failure. Turning away from the Quran in essence means purposely rejecting it. Make the learning, understanding, reciting, and implementation of the Quran the biggest priority in life – and do it now before it is too late!
